Recording summary

The agent began by mapping the packed layout. Each byte in w_q holds two values for the same output column: the low nibble is the even-K weight and the high nibble is the odd-K weight. With group size 128, each group contains 64 packed rows, plus one scale and zero-point per output column. A natural tile therefore loads 64 packed rows and dequantizes them within the GEMM kernel.

The agent explored assembling a full unpacked (BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N) weight tile. Triton’s tl.join adds a minor last dimension, and reshaping that result would interleave along the wrong axis for this layout. The agent instead derived the equivalent sum of two products: activation values at even K positions times low-nibble weights, plus activation values at odd K positions times high-nibble weights. Triton’s tl.split operates on a final dimension of size two, so reshaping the activation tile to (BLOCK_M, BLOCK_K/2, 2) gives the parity split directly.

The kernel’s core, as written in solution.py, was:

        w_lo = (w_packed & 0xF).to(tl.bfloat16)
        w_hi = (w_packed >> 4).to(tl.bfloat16)

        scales = tl.load(scales_ptr + g * stride_sk + offs_n * stride_sn)
        zeros_ = tl.load(zeros_ptr + g * stride_zk + offs_n * stride_zn)

        w_bf_lo = (w_lo - zeros_[None, :]) * scales[None, :]
        w_bf_hi = (w_hi - zeros_[None, :]) * scales[None, :]

        x_r = tl.reshape(x, (BLOCK_M, HALF_K, 2))
        x_even, x_odd = tl.split(x_r)

        acc = tl.dot(x_even, w_bf_lo, acc)
        acc = tl.dot(x_odd, w_bf_hi, acc)

The wrapper selected BLOCK_M as 16, 32, 64, or 128 based on M, with BLOCK_N=128 and BLOCK_K=GROUP_SIZE=128. The kernel kept the accumulator in FP32 and converted to BF16 for output. The model’s registered buffers matched the reference names and expected layouts.

Several help commands timed out; the agent switched to reading Triton’s installed source. That confirmed tl.split requires a last dimension of size two and that tl.join appends a minor dimension, supporting the separate-dot design.

MiniMax-M3 W4A16 GEMM on H100: official score 0.1011
Memory summary

MiniMax-M3 implemented W4A16 GEMM as a fused Triton kernel that unpacks each byte’s low and high nibbles, dequantizes them with groupwise bf16 scales and zero-points, and accumulates the products in one pass. The official H100 result passed correctness and scored 0.1011 peak fraction, rank 10 among 16 scored leaderboard entries.

Relevant prior context

The run confirmed an H100 PCIe target and found PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130, Triton 3.6.0, and CUDA 13.2; CUTLASS and bitsandbytes were unavailable. After an initial sanity-script failure caused by constructing a model with the wrong N for one shape, the script was corrected and all five shapes passed allclose(atol=0.1, rtol=0.1). The full correctness checker then passed. A quick benchmark showed roughly 42 µs per shape, while the in-trace official benchmark reported a peak fraction of 0.1014; the final official score was 0.1011.

Important non-obvious context

The packed weight layout is (K/2, N), with the even-K value in the low nibble and odd-K value in the high nibble. Scales and zero-points are (K/128, N), and each 128-wide K group is dequantized as (value - zero) * scale. The kernel uses two dot products per group after splitting the activation tile into even and odd K rows.

The official regime is memory, with H100 peak bandwidth recorded as 2039 GB/s. The leaderboard catalog and trace manifest both report verdict: unaudited and rejected: false; they do not contain a completed audit verdict. The task’s checker rejects specified prebuilt dequantization/GEMM operations, and the submitted implementation performs unpacking and multiplication in its own Triton kernel.

Recording summary

The solution fixes GROUP_SIZE = 128, uses BLOCK_N = 128 and BLOCK_K = 128, and chooses BLOCK_M based on M (16 for M≤16, 32 for M≤32, 64 for M≤64, otherwise 128). Each program handles one M/N tile and loops over K groups. Within a group, it loads the packed weight tile, extracts and dequantizes the two nibbles, splits the activation tile into even/odd K rows, and accumulates two tl.dot results before storing bf16 output. The launch uses four warps and three stages.

The core unpack and accumulation in the submitted solution:

w_lo = (w_packed & 0xF).to(tl.bfloat16)
w_hi = (w_packed >> 4).to(tl.bfloat16)

w_bf_lo = (w_lo - zeros_[None, :]) * scales[None, :]
w_bf_hi = (w_hi - zeros_[None, :]) * scales[None, :]

x_r = tl.reshape(x, (BLOCK_M, HALF_K, 2))
x_even, x_odd = tl.split(x_r)

acc = tl.dot(x_even, w_bf_lo, acc)
acc = tl.dot(x_odd, w_bf_hi, acc)
